name: Acute Myelomonocytic Leukemia

criteria.description: Presence of ≥20% myeloblasts and monoblasts in bone marrow or peripheral blood
Evidence of both granulocytic and monocytic differentiation in leukemic cells
Positive myeloperoxidase and nonspecific esterase staining in blasts
Expression of myeloid (CD13, CD33) and monocytic markers (CD14, CD11b)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: ≥20% blasts in marrow or blood with evidence of both granulocytic and monocytic differentiation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is based on morphology, cytochemistry, and immunophenotyping according to FAB criteria.

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear showing myeloblasts and monoblasts
Bone marrow biopsy with ≥20% blasts and myelomonocytic proliferation
Cytochemical staining positive for myeloperoxidase and nonspecific esterase
Complete blood count showing anemia, thrombocytopenia, and leukocytosis or leukopenia
imaging: Chest X-ray may show leukostasis-related infiltrates
genetic: Cytogenetic abnormalities such as inv(16)(p13q22) or t(16;16)(p13;q22) commonly associated
Molecular mutations including CBFβ-MYH11 fusion gene
other: Immunophenotyping confirming myeloid and monocytic markers

distinguishingFeatures: Predominance of monocytic cells (>80%) without significant granulocytic differentiation
Different immunophenotypic profile lacking granulocytic markers
Predominance of granulocytic differentiation without monocytic lineage involvement
Chronic course with persistent monocytosis >1x10^9/L for >3 months
Less than 20% blasts in blood and marrow

redFlags: Rapidly progressive cytopenias with bleeding and infections
Presence of >20% blasts in peripheral blood or bone marrow
Signs of leukostasis such as respiratory distress or neurological symptoms
references: Arber DA, et al. The 2016 revision to the World Health Organization classification of myeloid neoplasms and acute leukemia. Blood. 2016.
Swerdlow SH, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
